newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Metals - Singapore copper premiums seen easing.
newsitem.headline: Asia Metals - Singapore copper premiums seen easing.

text.p: Singapore base metal premiums were mainly stagnant in a dull regional market this week and copper premiums were expected to dip on falling demand in Southeast Asian countries, dealers said on Friday.

"Our orders from Thailand and Malaysia have been reduced by around 10-15 percent in recent months," one dealer said. "The electronic sector is not performing very well and output has been reduced, resulting in poor demand for copper."
Copper premiums were unchanged from last week at between a $3-$7 a tonne over London Metal Exchange (LME) cash prices, but traders said current quotes are faltering.
"Some sellers have indicated lower premiums, quoting at par," said one trader.
LME cash copper prices have eased from Thursday's $2,450 a tonne to around $2,368.

Referring to the narrowing backwardation or the cash to three months price differential and falling three-month LME prices, Asian traders said previous firm quotes were finally correcting downwards reflecting soft cash copper fundamentals in
the region.

Singapore zinc premiums have stabilised after slipping by about $10 a tonne a week ago on a rise in Chinese zinc supplies. "The zinc market is taking a breather," said one trader. "Stocks in the LME warehouse in Singapore will probably see a small rise (on Friday) as some more Chinese deliveries take place," he said.
Another trader said "(zinc) premiums are on the high side and should move lower as demand dwindles."
In the aluminium market, a small volume of around 1,000 tonnes has been traded into Vietnam and East Asia, said a dealer with a Japanese firm.
"Otherwise the market is also quiet with very little discussion and activities," he added.
One trader said business has already started to slow as most Asian traders have begun to wind down in preparation for approaching Chinese and Moslim festivities in early February.
